VERDICT: VESTIGIAL, deleted. Loop.Ack, its acked atomic.Bool and all three acked.Load() checks are gone (Ack was the field's only writer, so in production acked was permanently false and the checks were provably no-ops).

CALLERS PROVEN BY SEARCH, not by trusting the bead: repo-wide grep for 'Ack' and 'acked' over every file type. Only hits outside internal/reminder were .beads/interactions.jsonl (the jyi close note) and docs/plans/2026-02-27-urgtomat-reminder-implementation.md, a dated historical plan that still calls the project urgtomat. Sole production construction site is outstandingReminder.startLoopLocked (internal/core/outstanding.go:248), which never acked. An independent reviewer re-ran the sweep and agreed.

WHY NOT A MISSING CAPABILITY: 'the user answered this reminder' is already fully expressed. Core.onTransition (internal/core/core.go:97-105) documents it outright -- 'leaving any state answers whichever reminder was outstanding, morning included' -- and calls reminder.cancel(). ADR-004 frames a reminder as 'a repeating nudge... cancelled by an answer'. An answer in this product is not a separate dismiss gesture; it is the transition the nudge was asking for (start leaves Idle, confirm leaves AwaitingConfirm). The not-now cases are covered by suppress/skipToday. So nothing user-visible is lost.

STRONGER POINT found in review: Ack's documented semantics CONTRADICTED pinned behaviour. It stopped even the first alert, while loopNotify's promised flag and TestThePromisedFirstAlertSurvivesARetirementThatBeatsIt guarantee the first alert fires (ADR-007). Had anything called Ack it would have broken that promise -- exactly the 6->5 regression jyi recorded. This was not merely unused, it was a live contradiction of a pinned guarantee.

Also honours jyi's ruling that whether an alert counts belongs to the owner in outstandingReminder.ring, not to the loop. A second suppression switch inside Loop duplicated the owner's authority (ADR-004).

TESTS: TestLoopRepeatsUntilAck deleted (only exercised the removed API). Replaced by TestLoopRepeatsUntilItsContextIsCancelled covering ctx retirement, which this package had NO test for -- a net coverage gain. Proved it discriminates: mutating Loop.Run to ignore its ctx gives 'loop_test.go:38: loop kept running after its context was cancelled' FAIL, restored to PASS. First version of the test did NOT discriminate (a reachable MaxAlerts bound masked the cancel); fixed with MaxAlerts 1_000_000 plus a repeats<2 pre-assertion guarding the other direction. The three ADR-pinned core tests still pass.

Branch chore/remove-dead-apis, commit d378ddf. Not pushed.

DELETED as debris. Countdown.tickedStatusLine is gone, along with the two privates only it used (runningPhases, the #/\d{2,}:\d{2}/# clock regex).

CALLERS PROVEN BY SEARCH: repo-wide grep for 'tickedStatusLine' over every file type found only Countdown.swift itself, three CountdownTests cases, and .beads/interactions.jsonl. Zero production callers, confirming the bead. Also grepped 'statusLine' and 'status_line' repo-wide to map every reader. An independent reviewer re-ran the sweep and found zero hits for tickedStatusLine and runningPhases anywhere.

NO CAPABILITY LOST: the countdown the window actually draws is MainWindowContent.countdown via Countdown.formatRemaining, which is alive and untouched. tickedStatusLine spliced MM:SS into the daemon's status_line string, a surface the single-window client stopped rendering when ConnectionStatus dropped its state parameter.

TESTS: the three tickedStatusLine cases and their now-unused state(...) helper deleted (they only exercised the removed API). Verified no coverage lost: MainWindowContentTests.swift:65-84 already asserts the equivalent surviving behaviour on MainWindowContent.countdown(for:) -- running phases format, nil phaseEndAt, paused uses pausedRemaining, idle/awaitingConfirm nil. The formatRemaining tests, including the fi_FI locale pin, all survive. 559 XCTest cases pass (was 562).

DANGLING REFERENCES UPDATED: the enum doc claimed 'Local 1 Hz ticking of the daemon's status line' -- work the type no longer does; Ticker (Ticker.swift:10, .seconds(1)) owns the cadence, so it now says Countdown formats and Ticker drives. formatRemaining's doc and the fi_FI test's rationale both justified the en_US_POSIX pin by 'what clock matches above', a regex that no longer exists; both rewritten to the surviving reason (the TUI renders the same remaining time in unlocalized Go and the two surfaces can be open side by side). Verified docs/designs/native-macos-client.md:128 and :173 stay true -- clients still compute the countdown locally from phase_end_at. DESIGN.md's status-line entries are TUI-only, untouched. No ADR needed changing.

KEPT DELIBERATELY: DaemonState.statusLine. It is now the only zero-reader field in that struct, so on review it got a doc comment saying so -- it stays because it is part of the daemon's state document (internal/core/state.go:37, pinned by state_test.go:169) and StateDecodingTests pins that it still decodes, not because anything is waiting to use it. Without the comment it is a landmine for the next dead-code sweep. Countdown itself is not a husk: formatRemaining plus posixLocale still earn the namespace, with three call sites in MainWindowContent.

Branch chore/remove-dead-apis, commits b609749 and 2cd149a. Not pushed.
